sentences.text: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients The distress of the man on the other end of the video call was clear to dementia specialist nurse Louise Burns.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: He was struggling to get his elderly mum, who had the condition, out of hospital - she needed support to move into her home.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Burns was able to put him at ease.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: She is part of a team running virtual clinics that support more than 100 patients and family members a week: "No matter what stage they are at, we try to help," she says.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: She explained the discharge process and where to go for help.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The man's mother was soon back where she wanted to be.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Traditionally, a service like this would have been run by the National Health Service – but the clinic, which was set up during Covid and continued because of strong demand, is entirely funded by the charity Dementia UK.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The charity's chief nursing officer Paul Edwards says it is "trying to fill the gaps" within stretched NHS services.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Burns adds: "The NHS and social care are under such huge pressure and dementia cases are rising - it's not always easy to get the support you need." Dementia UK is just one of many charities working in the health sphere.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: From children's care to mental health and cancer services, charities are playing an increasingly important role in caring for patients.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: A desire from governments of different parties from the 1990s onwards to develop a market of providers – NHS, private and voluntary sector – has meant the charity sector is now big business in health.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: It's estimated that cancer charities alone raise more than £1bn a year, and the NHS in England spends nearly £2bn a year buying services from the not-for-profit and voluntary sector.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But there are concerns about the scale of charities' involvement in delivering frontline services - including from within the voluntary sector itself.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Those directly providing services say they are having to subsidise squeezed NHS budgets.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: And despite the good intentions of the charitable sector, some critics say its work with the NHS means more money ends up in wealthier communities.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Defenders of charities' involvement, however, say much-needed funding should be welcomed.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: So is the growing role of charities a symptom of a health service at breaking point - or a positive way of involving the public in their health care?
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: There's nothing new about UK health charities taking on a major role in delivering services.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Prior to 1948, British healthcare was provided through a patchwork of local charities, voluntary organisations, local authorities and private arrangements.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Many hospitals depended on charitable donations, subscriptions and fundraising events to survive.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The creation of the NHS transformed this model.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Most hospitals were brought into public ownership and funded through taxation.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: NHS founder Aneurin Bevan believed healthcare should not depend on charity, and restrictions were placed on NHS hospital charities actively raising money.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But they did not disappear completely - they could still receive gifts and donations.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: A major shift came with the Health Services Act 1980, which encouraged a more active fundraising culture.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: From then on, NHS charities expanded significantly and became increasingly professionalised.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: By the 1990s and beyond, they were raising substantial sums for equipment, buildings, research, and the likes of play areas in children's wards and well-equipped staff rooms.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Today, distinct from charities devoted to particular diseases or conditions, there are now more than 220 NHS charities attached to hospitals or community services, which raise £620m a year.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Ellie Orton, chief executive of NHS Charities Together, which represents them, says that while this sum may sound high, it represents only around 0.3% of the health budget.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: She says the very purpose of the charities is to provide support, equipment and services that are additional to what the NHS provides.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Recent schemes involve things like CPR training for members of the public, defibrillators being placed in community venues and green spaces in hospitals.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Scanners, blood transfusion equipment and emergency department co-ordinators have also been funded by charities.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Some would say say core NHS functions like these are exactly what we pay our taxes for.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "It's just the way it is now.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: We shouldn't get too ideological about this.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: It's not helpful to think the state can do everything.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Yes we pay taxes but that has to cover lots – and it's finite.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: In recent years, huge one-off sums have been raised.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: During the pandemic, the NHS Charities Together Covid appeal resulted in a £10m donation by the trading firm XTX Markets, while the Rausing family - best known for founding the food packaging giant Tetra Pak – gave £5m.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Rugby league legend Sir Kevin Sinfield's fundraising in support of his friend Rob Burrow helped bring in £6.8m for a specialist motor neurone disease centre at Leeds Teaching Hospitals.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "Of course, we are not talking about going back to a pre-1948 situation, but there is real interest in what such philanthropy can do," says Orton.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But there are inequalities.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The NHS charity sector is dominated by some of the big London hospitals and specialist cancer and children's centres.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The Royal Marsden and Great Ormond Street charities between them are responsible for nearly a sixth of the investment made by NHS charities.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "This does concern us," admits Orton.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: For example, over the past three decades, Dementia UK has developed a well-established network of specialist dementia nurses known as Admiral Nurses, who work in a range of hospital and community settings.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The model is based on the charity co-funding posts with the NHS for up to two years with the expectation that the NHS will then take on the funding.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But with demand increasing, Edwards says it is becoming a "struggle" to get the funding needed from the NHS or from donations.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "We are being asked to fund them for longer or find more than half the cost," he says.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "Services are really being cut back." And it is not just in dementia care that charities are noticing a squeeze.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: The charity WellChild has helped establish a network of 54 specialist nurses who work with very sick children.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: It funds these posts for the first three years, before responsibility for funding is expected to transfer to the NHS.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But disappointingly for the charity, for the first time this year a nurse post was not kept on, says Amy Mitchell, WellChild's director of programmes.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: What's more, WellChild's nurses are only meant to carry a caseloads of 15, but the average is currently 40.

sentences.text: The Palace of Westminster and wider parliamentary estate has a web of old cables in its basement (right) More asbestos has been discovered in Parliament, the BBC has learnt, as MPs come under pressure to sign off on a major revamp of the crumbling home of UK democracy.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: Known asbestos items in the Palace of Westminster and wider parliamentary estate, such as insulation, roofing, floor tiles and ropes, now number more than 1,650 - an increase of 500 since 2021.

sentences.text: It comes as the government considers holding a vote on refurbishing Parliament, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years, after years of indecision and delay.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for Parliament's restoration, with every additional year of delay costing taxpayers £420m.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: More asbestos items were found during surveys in preparation for the long-awaited refurbishment project, parliamentary authorities said.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: Asbestos has been identified as one of the main reasons for the refurbishment, given the dangers to human health when its fibres are airborne.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: While asbestos is largely fireproof, surrounding fire and heat can release fibres over long distances.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: In the past five years, 700 items of asbestos have been removed from Parliament but the total has still risen, a Freedom of Information request by the BBC found.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: Under Health and Safety Executive guidelines, most of it is classed as low risk in concealed areas, meaning it is less likely to be disturbed, but almost 200 items are classed as medium risk meaning they may require remedial works.
sentences.article_title: Parliament faces 'grave risks' as more asbestos discovered ahead of revamp decision

sentences.text: A spokesperson for UK Parliament said its "absolute priority is the safety of the those who work on and visit the parliamentary estate" with improved asbestos monitoring, new awareness training, and plans to further remove it.

sentences.text: "Alice was well aware of the risks relating to asbestos and mesothelioma," he added.

sentences.text: This school protester in Paris called on the government to "tax the rich, not our futures" on Thursday Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow vest" movement and workers.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: The five unions have combined forces across the public and private sector, with demands for higher wages to combat the cost of living and protected public services.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said that 70,000 police and gendarmes are being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: More than 250 separate actions are planned for 5 November, with some disruption reported in schools, hospitals and public transport.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic , which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Thursday's march will be allowed through the centre of Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: Instead, the march is set to follow another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: The CFDT union complained that getting court approval for the route only on Wednesday evening made organising the march more difficult.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: The last big mobilisation at the weekend passed off with relatively little violence, and the interior minister said the police deployment would be on a similar scale on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

sentences.text: A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk.

sentences.text: London-based Xyra Group has offered to pay off half of Poundland's outstanding debts - a key sticking point in takeover talks so far - immediately.

sentences.text: The rest would be deferred.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has ruled out reparations but is open to a formal apology The UK has signed up to "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith" talks that address the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, Commonwealth leaders in Antigua have said.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: The 18 page document , external includes a paragraph in which the leaders "welcome the agreement of the Government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms".
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened the door to a formal apology on behalf of the UK for its role in the slave trade, while ruling out the prospect of reparations.

sentences.text: James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas' Senate race, ending a 38-year Democratic losing streak in statewide elections there.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: In South Carolina, Annie Andrews beat Darline Graham, who had been appointed to the seat after the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Few analysts had that seat in play even a few months ago.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Five-term Republican Susan Collins conceded Maine's Senate election to Democrat Troy Jackson.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Paralympian Josh Turek flipped the Iowa Senate seat held by retiring Republican Senator Joni Ernst.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democrats also wrested from Republicans a Senate seat in Ohio, with Sherrod Brown's comeback victory over Jon Husted.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has beaten Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's bitterly fought Senate race.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Nor was that the end of the electoral carnage for Republicans.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Ruby-red Texas witnessed another seismic result in the governor's race.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa ousted the incumbent Republican Greg Abbott, who was earlier this year seen as the prohibitive favourite.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democrats also took governors' races in Iowa, Ohio and Georgia, which made history by electing the first black woman to such a post.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the party has won a House majority for the first time since 2022.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: They are projected to win 245 House seats and the Republicans 166 seats.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democrats celebrate in Maine where the party won a crucial Senate race A look at the key races offers plenty of reasons why.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democrats flipped House seats in Texas, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Iowa, Kentucky and Colorado, among others.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: And they were poised to make gains in Virginia and Indiana.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Black Democrats in the southern states turned out in record number, helping to carry their party to victory.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: And Hispanic voters, whose support had helped secure Trump's presidential victory in 2024, swung decisively back to the Democrats.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Democrats won all three House races in the overwhelmingly Hispanic congressional districts along the Texas-Mexico border.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: And Hispanic voters helped Democrats hold House seats in Florida that the state's Republicans had sought to flip by redrawing the congressional district lines.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: In fact, the congressional redistricting battles that had dominated headlines for months last year ended up being a bust for the Republicans.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: In Texas, they had hoped their line-drawing would net five new seats for their party.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: But on Tuesday they may end up losing one seat.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: If there is a silver lining for conservatives, Florida as a whole still appears to tilt to the right.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Republican Senator Ashley Moody narrowly won re-election, as did congressman Byron Donalds, who was elected the Sunshine State's first black governor.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: And embattled Republicans were able to hold governorships in Vermont and New Hampshire.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: But the bright spots were few and far between.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: Just two years ago, Trump won the presidency with 48% of the vote.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: He claimed an electoral mandate.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: He then went about governing like it, pushing sometimes unpopular policies on trade and immigration, and launching an Iran war that is opposed by most of the American public.
sentences.article_title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

sentences.text: On Tuesday, voters gave him the kind of stinging rebuke that will not be easily forgotten.

sentences.text: It was an unlikely greeting to hear at a Democratic Party victory rally after the US midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Abdul El-Sayed , 42, born to Egyptian immigrant parents, playfully addressed Vice-President JD Vance, who had campaigned against him but will now swear him into office in January as Michigan's new Senator.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: The US-born Democrat spent much of his campaign fending off attacks from conservative media and President Donald Trump, who accused him of supporting the Muslim Brotherhood.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: El-Sayed rejected the allegations.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: "My name is Abdul Rahman Mohammed El-Sayed," he said in an Egyptian Arabic accent to the cheering crowd at his victory rally.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: His Arabic Muslim name was a target for many of his opponents.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: He is set to become the first Muslim senator.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: El-Sayed ran a social media-first campaign, with TikTok edits showing him speaking directly to young voters, tapping into Gen Z humour, and sporting friendship bracelets.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: The former public health administrator's campaign centred on a progressive agenda, including Medicare for All, affordable housing and curbing corporate influence in politics.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: He has also been a vocal critic of US military aid to Israel.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: But El-Sayed was not alone.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: From an Ethiopian-born Gen Z congresswoman to candidates with Nigerian heritage, several other politicians with African roots won in this year's midterms.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: The elections, held halfway through a president's four-year term, decide who represents Americans in Congress, as well as in thousands of state and local offices.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Born in Addis Ababa, Melat Kiros' family moved to Denver when she was a baby At 29, Melat Kiros became the first Gen Z woman elected to the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Born in Ethiopia, she arrived in the US as a baby and grew up in Denver.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: She had never held elected office before defeating a 15-term incumbent in Colorado's 1st District in the Democrat primary before winning a landslide in Tuesday's election.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Kiros, like El-Sayed, campaigned on issues that have become central to young progressive voters: the cost of living, universal childcare and Medicare for All.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America, she has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and ending US military aid to Israel.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Her outspoken criticism of Israel's war in Gaza has attracted controversy.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Kiros has said her criticism is directed at the Israeli state, not Jewish people.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: She was fired from a top New York law firm in 2023 after she refused to take down an open letter to dozens of law firms who had urged law school deans to crack down on antisemitism on campuses as students engaged in pro-Palestinian protests.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Kiros condemned antisemitism, but warned the law firms, including the one she worked for, against conflating "such bigotry with the geo-political question of Israel's legitimacy".
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: She said she started thinking more seriously about politics in general after being fired.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Adrian Boafo's parents moved from Ghana to the US Adrian Boafo, meanwhile, a second-generation Ghanaian-American, will represent Maryland's 5th Congressional District after succeeding veteran Congressman Steny Hoyer, who retired after a political career spanning more than four decades.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: The 32-year-old was born in Virginia and raised in Prince George's County, Maryland.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: His parents immigrated to the US from Ghana.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Boafo's route to Congress began in local politics.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: He served on the Bowie City Council before becoming a Maryland state delegate in 2023.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: He also worked for Hoyer before eventually winning the race to replace him.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: His campaign focused on the cost of living, childcare and protecting federal workers, a major issue in a district close to Washington DC and home to thousands of government employees.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: In his victory statement, Boafo said representing his constituents had "never felt more urgent", pointing to federal job cuts, rising costs and the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Among those returning to Congress is Somali-born Ilhan Omar, 44, who won a fifth term despite an ongoing federal investigation.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Federal agents searched her Washington home in October as part of an investigation into her immigration paperwork.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Omar has denied wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: First elected to Congress in 2018, Omar became the first Somali-American and one of the first Muslim women to serve in the chamber.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: She has also been a frequent target of President Trump, who has repeatedly criticised her and other Somali immigrants.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Trump has previously used derogatory language to describe some African countries, including Somalia.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: In October, his Yemeni-born adviser Amer Ghalib said the president would refrain from using such language.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Others made their breakthroughs in state and local politics.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Junior Ezeonu was born in Nigeria and moved to the US as a young child.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: By 27, he had already become Grand Prairie's youngest city council member before winning a seat in the Texas State House.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: Then there is Carol Kazeem , 34, a Pennsylvania state legislator of Nigerian heritage who has retained her seat at District 159.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: At least four candidates with Nigerian heritage won in the 3 November midterms.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: For some young Africans watching from across the Atlantic, these victories have offered a glimpse of what a new generation of voters could achieve at home.
sentences.article_title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms

sentences.text: DR Congo has been facing the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: It is not clear when the flight will take place.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: "Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low." There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: It has since become the deadliest in the country's history, with a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Ebola can result in serious illness and death.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Early symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea but it can progress to organ failure and internal bleeding.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: The ongoing outbreak centred on DR Congo is fueled by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: There is no approved vaccine but the World Health Organisation said experts have recommended adding two new candidate drugs to an ongoing clinical trial.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: The vaccines, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and another by the firm Moderna, will join the trial once they are approved by Congolese health authorities.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: It will be the first time jabs specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak.
sentences.article_title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK

sentences.text: Since the outbreak, Ebola cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

sentences.text: Arif Patel, who masterminded a massive VAT carousel fraud, remains on the run One of the UK's most prolific tax fraudsters has lost his appeal against a judge's order to repay more than £90m he gained through his crimes.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Arif Patel, from Preston, ran an international organised crime group, which stole tens of millions of pounds of public money through a complex tax fraud.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: He fled the UK in 2011 and has never returned, but was eventually convicted in his absence of offences including conspiracies to cheat His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC), the importation and sale of counterfeit goods and money- laundering.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: In a written judgment on Tuesday, the Court of Appeal rejected his claim that the size of his property empire, which had been seized by the court-appointed receiver in 2010, had not kept pace with inflation and that the judge's order had been disproportionate.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: In 2023, Patel was given a 20-year jail sentence but hasn't served a day of his sentence.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Following his convictions a judge issued a confiscation order, which said he must repay £90.5m.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: But despite being on the run in Dubai, Patel was able to bring a case to the Court of Appeal in London, to argue the sum was excessive.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Following Patel's conviction the judge ruled between 2003 and 2008, he'd made £52.7m through his crimes, which included £33.4m of taxpayers' money he stole through VAT fraud, and more than £19m made from the large-scale importation and sale of fake designer goods.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: But when the confiscation order was made in 2025, that figure had been increased to £90.5m to account for inflation.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The fugitive fraudster who stole from you The judgment said Patel would not have faced a significantly larger total sum had he "accepted at the outset his criminality, disclosed his criminal benefits and agreed to forfeit them".
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Patel's legal team also argued Patel did not have assets to cover this amount, an argument which was also rejected.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The judgment said Patel "appears to have been able to live in very comfortable circumstances in the UAE for 15 years without identified means of support".
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: It added the judge who made the original confiscation order was entitled to conclude that by the time Patel absconded in 2011, he would have had "many millions of truly hidden assets".
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The judgment also revealed Patel had failed to cooperate with an official receiver whose job it was to identify his assets in Dubai.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: "I gather that the applicant procured the receiver's arrest when he went to the UAE," the judgment said.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Work will now begin to sell off Patel's property empire.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The funds raised will be returned to the public purse.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: A judge ordered Patel's Ferrari Superamerica to be auctioned off But behind the facade, Patel was at the helm of one of the country's biggest ever VAT frauds, known as a carousel fraud.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: A carousel fraud involves chains of fake business transactions created as a way of stealing VAT repayments from HMRC.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Goods are moved between different companies, in and out of the country, to generate false tax refunds.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The same shipments of goods are often moved around repeatedly, hence the name carousel fraud.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Patel's criminal empire was uncovered in a series of raids in 2008, which followed a years long investigation by HMRC and Lancashire Police.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Last month File on 4 Investigates revealed Patel's glamorous life in Dubai, and his claims that he had made sizeable donations to charitable organisations.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: The BBC tried to contact Patel for comment through his Manchester-based solicitor, but received no response.
sentences.article_title: On-the-run fraudster loses £90m confiscation appeal

sentences.text: Leanne Duff says it was "carnage" inside her property after an Airbnb stay An Airbnb host has described being too upset to return to her own home after it was trashed during a party.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Leanne Duff, from Plymouth, Devon, said she felt "violated" after every room in her house was damaged in April, including her 13-year-old son's bedroom.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: She said food was smeared over the walls, internal doors were removed and stacked in a room, a TV was smashed and her son's electric guitar had its strings cut and his toys ripped.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Airbnb said it had removed a teenager who booked the property from its platform and reimbursed Duff the cost of damage to the property, while police said they could not prove among those present who caused it.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: The minimum age to create an account and book a property on Airbnb is 18 and the firm said hosts and guests must complete an identity verification process.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Airbnb said "no verification system is foolproof" but identity checks across the platform were "designed to help users have greater confidence that people on Airbnb are who they say they are".
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Airbnb reimbursed the cost of damage to the property, including a broken TV More news stories for Devon Listen to the latest news for Devon Duff, who rents out her home when she is not there to supplement her income, has been a host for seven years and has 200 positive reviews.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: She said she had never had an issue before but knew something was amiss when she returned to the property to notice her window was wide open and her sofa cushions in the street.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Recalling when she stepped inside, she said: "I can only be described it as carnage.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: "Doors had been taken off their hinges and carried upstairs, food from my cupboard had been cooked and thrown at and smeared on the walls, the TV was smashed, my clothes were ripped, all the drawers had been opened and my jewellery had been thrown everywhere.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: "I was stunned, shocked and heartbroken.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: They didn't steal anything though." Duff says the experience left her feeling nervous about people's intentions Food was removed from cupboards and left strewn around the property Duff called police and went to stay with her mother while an investigation was carried out.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: She has since heightened her vetting and no longer rents her house for just one night.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.article_title: Airbnb host felt 'violated' after house trashed

sentences.text: Almost all the front pages carry the results of the US midterm elections, where President Donald Trump's Republican Party is suffering heavy defeats and will lose control of Congress.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Crushing midterm rebuke to Trump" is the Financial Times' verdict, embedding a tally of the results so far - which show the Democrats winning majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Anger over cost of living spurs Democratic blue wave" the paper says, providing its business-focused audience a taste of the market reaction by reporting "oil prices tumble and tech hyperscalers' shares surge".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Daily Telegraph focuses on the blame-shifting, saying Vice President JD Vance "turns on Trump" and "blames Iran war" after the "Republicans' humiliating midterm election defeat".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: It quotes the "defiant" president after he said: I'll do it all again", according to the paper.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Telegraph also notes some of the Democrats' breakthroughs on the "record-breaking" night, including its victory in Kansas which it explains "had not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Trump faces backlash as Democrats make history" says the headline in the Times - placing a photo of James Talarico, the successful Senate Democratic candidate in Texas, placing a hand across his chest in front of his supporters at his victory rally, celebrating a feat not seen "for nearly 40 years".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: It says the "president's opponents" have "captured seven Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and, in the biggest prize of the night, in Texas".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Vance blames Trump's war for crushing defeat" continues the i Paper.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Blue wave sweeps America - washing away Maga candidates", the paper concludes, although it adds comments from the White House: "Trump is still your President".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "The daggers were out for Donald Trump" says the Daily Mail, writing: "JD Vance and even Don Jr blame President's Iran War debacle for poll wipeout".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Mail also highlights a piece from its veteran columnist Richard Littlejohn under the headline "A Republican friend tells me: "Trump's crazy, he's capable of anything now - even starting WWIII".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Trumped" is the Guardian's single-word headline.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: Americans "woke up to a radically altered political landscape", the paper says, as a "new era on Capitol Hill dawned".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Lame Donald Duck" says the Metro, teasing the president using the "lame duck" refrain that appears on multiple front pages, crediting the insult to the victory speech of "Democrat big-hitter Jon Ossoff", who won his Senate race in Georgia, who the paper nominates as "a likely 2028 presidential challenger".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Trump dumped" says the Independent.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "American voters rebuke president over Iran war and hand Congress to Democrats in historic election upset," it reports.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The lyrics sung by Frank Sinatra in My Way endure on the front page of the Daily Star, which says that Trump "faces final curtain", concluding "and now the end is near".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Star also shows the president holding a microphone with a speech bubble proclaiming: "I did it Maga way".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Daily Mirror revives Bruce Springstein with: "Reborn in the U.S.A." writing that "Americans stood up to their bullying president and said no to hatred and lies".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: Switching focus from the midterms in the US, the Sun tops with a report on Thomas Markle Snr, the father of the Duchess of Sussex.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: "Markle filth stash no3" says its headline, writing that the FBI is to "search Hollywood lock-ups" as they "investigate a potential third cache of child abuse images".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: Markle has strongly denied possessing any such images.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: It comes after a government minister says "the planned sites to house asylum seekers will be 'away from communities'," according to the paper.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The fallout from the US midterm elections features on most of the morning's front pages, including the Financial Times , external , which says Americans delivered a "crushing rebuke" to Donald Trump, after a campaign dominated by the spiralling cost of living.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: The Daily Mail , external agrees, arguing voters passed a "damning verdict" on the president because they were "enraged" by high inflation and rising fuel prices.

sentences.text: According to the Daily Mirror , external , Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan "despite a vile smear campaign" after voters grew sick of the president's "bullying" and "narcissism".

sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Crushing midterm rebuke' and 'Trumped'

sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.

sentences.text: The so-called "quiet quitting" trend where workers do the basic requirements of a job but refuse to do anything more might be hitting the economy, analysis has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Over the last decade, Britons have become less engaged with the jobs they do and are less willing to put in extra effort, according to a Resolution Foundation report.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: The thinktank said this could partly help explain the slump in productivity since the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: "This is self-evidently bad for workers, but it also doesn't bode well for productivity and labour supply, both of which are vital for lifting living standards in the years ahead," said Hannah Slaughter, principal economist at the Resolution Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Quiet quitting was popularised on social media shortly after the pandemic .
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Frustrated by high demands, low pay, and a squeeze in living standards, many online posts said workers should only do what their bosses asked and nothing more.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: So you still show up for work, but no more helping out with additional tasks or checking emails outside work hours, instead focusing on work-life balance and "acting your wage".
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Meanwhile, those who were not even "fairly" satisfied with their roles has sunk to one-in-four, the lowest level on record.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: In addition, workers are less likely than 10 years ago to say they have an interesting job, with 63% of those surveyed saying so, down from 74%.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: "Workers today are indeed a little less committed to their employers, and a little less intrinsically drawn to work in general, than workers were a decade ago," the report added.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: This shift over the last decade "may have contributed to weak productivity growth", which has slowed since the financial crisis and weakened again after the pandemic, the Resolution Foundation found.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Workers were also more focused on pay than in the past, which it said was "perhaps unsurprising... given the flatlining living standards of the past decade".
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Sir John Curtice, politics professor and co-editor of the report, said the analysis does not mean that young people have "become more 'work-shy', nor have workers in general become more reluctant to change jobs".

sentences.text: Dan Harrison previously said his leaked remarks had been taken out of context The Reform UK leader of Leicestershire County Council has announced he is standing down after comments he made about staff redundancies were leaked online.

sentences.text: The Union flag was flown outside Tiananmen Gate, during Sir Keir Starmer's visit to Beijing in 2026 The government has failed to deliver on its promise to pursue a consistent approach towards China and is instead making up policy "as it goes along", MPs on the business committee have said.

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs

sentences.article_title: Can you tell ferritin levels from your face?

sentences.text: Lucy says she noticed changes in her skin and hair (left photo) alongside symptoms including fatigue and hair loss when her ferritin levels were low.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lighting and shadows also play a part "Do you have ferritin face?" a young woman asks on TikTok, pointing to dark circles, washed-out skin and brittle hair, alongside before-and-after style photographs.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: The content creator puts these features down to her iron levels.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: It is one of a growing number of videos and posts on TikTok and Instagram claiming that low ferritin - a protein which stores iron in the body - can leave visible clues on your face.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Users list pale or grey-looking skin, dark under-eye circles, dry or cracked lips, hair shedding and weak nails, while others share portraits claiming stark visual differences.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: The phrase "ferritin face" has spread widely across social media, with videos attracting millions of views.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But doctors say appearance alone cannot diagnose iron deficiency.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "Ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis," said GP Dr Aziza Sesay, who is based in the West Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on." Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Your ferritin levels show how good your body's iron stores are, while haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells which carries oxygen.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: When haemoglobin is low, the blood cannot carry as much oxygen - a condition known as anaemia.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But iron stores can become depleted before that happens, meaning someone can be iron-deficient and have symptoms without being anaemic.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Can you tell your ferritin levels from your face?
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "You've got no stored iron but you're maintaining your haemoglobin.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: That's the big disconnect," said consultant haematologist Dr Drew Provan.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Dr Sue Pavord, also a consultant haematologist, said iron deficiency is common and often under-diagnosed in women.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: UK guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology say ferritin below 15 micrograms per litre indicates absent iron stores, while below 30 generally indicates low iron stores.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Social media users have shared posts and videos claiming that low ferritin can cause visible changes to the face Lucy M, 32, who posts about hair loss as @marvluceskin on Instagram and TikTok, said "ferritin face" seemed to describe changes she had noticed in herself.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: In 2021 she developed heart palpitations, fatigue and hair loss.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: After being told her blood tests were normal and being diagnosed with generalised anxiety disorder, a later test showed her ferritin was 12 micrograms per litre.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lucy said she looked "grey" and her hair had become dull and brittle.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: She shared photographs with the BBC from when her ferritin was low, compared to when it had recovered, and said the difference between how she felt and looked was "night and day".
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Videos about "ferritin face" often encourage viewers to look for a combination of physical signs - from dark circles and pale skin to dry lips, thinning hair and brittle nails - and compare them with their own appearance.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "You're not ugly, your ferritin is low", one creator says, pointing to the camera.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Provan said it was "impossible" to determine someone's ferritin levels from how their face looks.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: People who are significantly anaemic may look pale, he explained, while fatigue can contribute to dark circles, but these visual signs are "subjective and unreliable".
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: In people with darker skin, changes in skin colour may be less obvious, Sesay added, meaning someone looking specifically for the signs described online could miss iron deficiency.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Doctors say appearance alone cannot tell you whether your ferritin is low, and that iron deficiency should be confirmed with a blood test For doctors, symptoms and how someone feels are more useful than appearance.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Blood tests matter not only to confirm iron deficiency, Provan and Sesay said, but to establish the cause and guide treatment.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Both said treatment should also address the cause.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Heavy periods, low dietary iron, gastrointestinal blood loss and problems absorbing iron through the gut can all play a role.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Iron deficiency is commonly treated with oral iron.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Pavord said iron tablets are best taken on an empty stomach, ideally first thing in the morning, and advised avoiding tea or coffee around the time they are taken because they can inhibit iron absorption.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Iron can also be obtained naturally from foods including meat, beans, lentils, leafy green vegetables and fortified cereals.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Taking iron supplements without a diagnosis can be harmful, while self-treating could delay the investigation of an underlying problem.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lucy said social media has nevertheless helped women take symptoms more seriously, and has given some the confidence to ask questions when something feels wrong.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "There are so many women saying, 'Oh my gosh, this is me," she said, adding that she is not a doctor and presents her content as her own experience.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: For her, doing so has been empowering - giving women information with which to advocate for themselves.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Sesay called social media a "double-edged sword" - it can encourage people to seek help, but can also lead them to incorrectly diagnose themselves from a short video.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: For Lucy, the useful part is not diagnosing yourself from your appearance, but knowing when something doesn't feel right, and when to ask questions.
