sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.

sentences.text: Plans to overhaul services are opposed by local communities Proposals to cut community hospital beds in some of Wales' most rural areas have met with strong resistance.

sentences.text: The maternity unit at the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital could become the only one in the county The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said it was concerned by reports that two maternity units could close.

sentences.text: Norfolk has maternity units at hospitals in Norwich, Gorleston and King's Lynn, with the latter two also serving Cambridgeshire and Suffolk.

sentences.text: The trade union posted on Facebook , external that local maternity services should be invested in rather than cut.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group (NWUHG) has set out its "Case for Change" , external on how services could be delivered in future, but stressed that no decisions had been made and no consultation had begun.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: NHS leaders said any move to concentrate services at one or two sites would be based on providing safer care for women and babies.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Documents show , external that some women that would currently give birth in Gorleston would face a two-hour public transport journey to get to alternative hospitals However, the RCM warned that closing units serving rural and isolated communities could mean women travelling "unacceptable distances" while in labour.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: If maternity services were removed from hospitals, the union said neonatal units and children's inpatient wards would also close because the services were inter-dependent.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Options include keeping services as they are, or closing consultant-led maternity units at the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston, the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn, or both.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: As well as women in Norfolk, the plans could affect women in Lowestoft and north Suffolk who give birth in Gorleston and those in Wisbech and north-east Cambridgeshire who travel to King's Lynn.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The RCM argued the proposals risked worsening existing inequalities in maternity outcomes and said the answer was investment and more staffing, rather than allowing services to "shrink".

sentences.text: Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.

sentences.text: A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it .

sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Like a lot of other holidays, food often plays a big part in how people celebrate Halloween, but it can be a more complex to navigate if you have a food allergy - especially if you want to go to parties or take children trick or treating.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: How do people with allergies ensure they can take part in the fun and stay safe?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And how can you help make sure that everyone is included in the celebrations?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, is allergic to milk and eggs.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "You have to make sure you read every packet of everything, and you couldn't eat anything until you got home so that you were safe and you were sure of what was happening," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: When it comes to Halloween, she said people having more awareness would mean that everyone could be included in the fun.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She says that her friend group really help her by knowing about her allergies and what to do if she was to have a reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Whilst she said it "wasn't easy" or a "particularly enjoyable" thing to do, she taught her group what to do in an emergency situation.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, went to a Halloween party this week dressed as Daphne from Scooby Doo Ciara carries EpiPens.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: These are adrenaline injections that can help to save people's lives in a serious allergic reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: The 15-year-old explained that Halloween can be a bit more difficult to navigate.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She described how a lot of people are helpful and understanding about allergies but sometimes, "there are other people that just don't seem to fully understand the consequences" of what would happen if she was exposed to what she's allergic to.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Her mum, Claire McGuigan, said she is proud of how well Ciara deals with her allergy.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She explained that parents of children with allergies have all the usual worries but "first and foremost is your allergy".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "As a parent, you carry all that worry and you just hope that they go out and they have a nice time and they come back safe, full of fun, and they can forget about their allergies as much as they can for that night".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think having a good circle of friends who understands the allergies is important.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Trying to prevent the harm rather than relying on the rescue medication is really, really important," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara's mum described the emotional burden on families and called for a national conversation about it.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said people who have children with allergies or have allergies themselves have to do their "best to navigate a whole world that wasn't designed for you".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think take your wins everyday that you're safe and that you're happy and don't let it define you.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: You can be who you want to be," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She believes that with "a bit of careful planning" children with allergies can feel included.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán in his Halloween costume Caolán has just turned 11.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: His mum Colette Donaghy said he does all the "school activities that you could name" and he's "mad into scooting".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán is allergic to nuts, dairy and eggs and has had, in the past, a very serious anaphylactic reaction that resulted in him being in an induced coma in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "He has an awareness and a knowledge and probably a risk awareness that many other children of his age wouldn't have," his mum said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She thinks it's important that children with allergies are "understood" but not made  to feel "really different".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán's mum, Colette Donaghy, said giving out individually wrapped sweets to trick-or-treaters could help avoid cross-contamination When it comes to Halloween, Donaghy explained that when Caolán trick or treats, he waits until the end when all the other children have been given their sweets.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Then he will explain to the people at the door that he has allergies and there's only certain things he can have.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And then, of course, before he would eat anything, we would have to check it," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy advised giving out individually wrapped sweets to help avoid cross-contamination.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She also suggested looking at alternatives to sweets like fruit or little toys "that don't cost very much".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "There's loads of different options for people and that would take away another layer of anxiety for parents," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy also explained how some people use teal pumpkins to indicate that a house will offer treats that are suitable for any trick-or-treaters who have any food allergies or intolerances.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Niamh Kennedy, from Food Allergy NI, said everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive Niamh Kennedy has three children who have food allergies and she is the chair of Food Allergy NI.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: It's a group aiming to build a safer and more inclusive society for everyone affected by food allergies.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said special occasions are often centred around food.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "For families living with food allergies, these celebrations can bring an extra layer of planning and worry that many people never have to think about." She explained that "every item may need to be checked and every situation assessed for risk".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Kennedy suggests that everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said this may include "offering non-food alternatives, providing clear ingredient information, communicating with families in advance and being mindful of the risk of cross-contact".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Being thoughtful and understanding can make a real difference to whether someone feels left out or included in these occasions." sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Air pollution is an annual problem in Delhi and large parts of northern India Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality to India's capital.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The city's air quality index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Authorities have responded by invoking Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), introducing measures to curb dust, vehicle emissions and other sources of pollution.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: GRAP is a set of emergency measures that become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The latest restrictions include more intensive road cleaning, higher parking charges to discourage private vehicle use and increased public transport services.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Delhi Metro has introduced 20 additional weekday train trips, while authorities have been directed to stagger government office timings to ease traffic congestion.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Officials said the measures were introduced after forecasts suggested air quality would remain very poor over the coming days.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Delhi and neighbouring parts of northern India grapple with hazardous air every winter, particularly around Diwali, one of India's biggest festivals, which is just days away.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The festival is celebrated with lights, lamps and fireworks, which often worsen the city's already poor air quality by releasing fine particles and harmful gases into the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The annual pollution crisis is driven by a combination of factors, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, falling temperatures, low wind speeds and the burning of crop stubble in neighbouring states.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The sharp rise in pollution follows an unusually clean October, when Delhi recorded its lowest average AQI for the month in eight years.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Experts have attributed the sudden deterioration to falling temperatures, slow winds and an increase in crop-residue burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: A recent storm had brought rain and stronger winds, helping clear the air.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: But as the weather settled, northwesterly winds returned, carrying smoke from burning fields towards the capital.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: India's pollution watchdog classifies AQI readings between 301 and 400 as "very poor", while anything above 400 is considered "severe".
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: On Wednesday morning, Delhi's AQI stood at 377.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The index takes into account eight major pollutants, including PM2.5 - tiny particles about 30 times smaller than the width of a human hair that can penetrate deep into the lungs.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Firecrackers set off during Diwali release particulate matter and gases into the air, adding to the existing pollution With Diwali just days away, there are concerns that fireworks could push pollution levels even higher.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Last year, Delhi woke up to a toxic haze the morning after the festival, despite a court directive to use less-polluting firecrackers.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Authorities have imposed restrictions on firecrackers over the years, including outright bans on their manufacture, sale and use, but enforcing them has proved difficult.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: On Monday, India's Supreme Court allowed the manufacture, sale and use of certified green firecrackers in Delhi and neighbouring areas for a limited period.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: It said the crackers could be set off only between 06:00 and 07:00 local time (00:30-01:30 GMT) and between 20:00 and 22:00 (14:30-16:30 GMT) on 7 and 8 November, during the Diwali weekend.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The court also banned fireworks within 300m of hospitals, care homes, schools and other designated silence zones.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Green firecrackers use modified chemical formulations designed to produce fewer emissions than conventional fireworks.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: They must carry QR codes that allow buyers and authorities to verify details of their manufacturer and certification.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: But ensuring that only approved firecrackers are sold remains a major challenge.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: In its latest order, the Supreme Court acknowledged that conventional firecrackers had continued to be sold as green alternatives, even when a complete ban was in place.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Even Mumbai, India's financial capital, has recorded very high levels of pollution in recent days It has directed police to patrol designated sales areas, carry out random QR-code checks and seize illegal firecrackers.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: During particularly severe pollution episodes, Delhi authorities have also introduced measures such as hybrid schooling, work-from-home arrangements and restrictions on certain vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The problem is not confined to the capital.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Mumbai, India's financial hub, has also recorded elevated pollution levels over the past month, despite benefiting from coastal winds that typically help disperse pollutants.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: On 24 October, Mumbai's AQI had reached 322, placing it in the "very poor" category.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The spike was attributed to a combination of low wind speeds, construction dust, garbage burning, firecracker emissions and pollutants carried from neighbouring regions.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The city's air quality has improved in recent days - and it recorded an AQI of 89, classified as "satisfactory", on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Neighbouring Navi Mumbai recorded a "moderate" AQI of 118.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: The improvement follows nearly two weeks of smoggy conditions, with residents sharing photos and videos of the haze on social media.
sentences.article_title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

sentences.text: Satish Acharya is among Indian cartoonists whose work has been restricted by Meta recently For the second time in three weeks, Indian cartoonist Satish Acharya found himself effectively invisible on Instagram in his own country.
sentences.article_title: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted

sentences.text: The 55-year-old discovered on Tuesday that his account had once again been briefly blocked in India, allegedly with no explanation from the platform.
sentences.article_title: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted

sentences.text: Just a few weeks ago, another cartoonist, Manjul, had found that Instagram had restricted a post criticising India's election commission over its controversial revision of voter rolls.
sentences.article_title: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted

sentences.text: His profile remained accessible.
sentences.article_title: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted

sentences.text: This video can not be played The zeptoverse explained by BBC science correspondent Pallab Ghosh Scientists have picked up signals from the smallest scale of nature ever explored – 100 billion times smaller than an atom.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: A world so small that some physicists have nicknamed it the zeptoverse.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The research, led by scientists based in Cambridge, was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Many sub-atomic particles are created by smashing the insides of atoms together Dark matter makes up a large part of our cosmos, and yet researchers have struggled to detect it.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Scientists know it is there because its gravitational force influences normal matter, but in all other respects it has remained completely invisible.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: So in this experiment, particles were smashed together at high energy and scientists studied the material that was thrown out - the shrapnel of collisions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: One of these is a sub-atomic particle - smaller than an atom - called a beauty quark.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The particle is unstable and exists for just one and a half trillionths of a second before breaking down into other forms - decaying.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Despite its short lifetime, researchers managed to detect it interacting with other tiny particles at a scale of a billion-trillionth of a metre.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Some theories suggest that at these scales particles are more sensitive to dark matter and it could influence how the quarks interact and break down.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: So, detecting activity in this tiny world could help scientists detect dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "We're knocking on the door of this zeptoverse," Dr Harry Cliff, of Cambridge University who led the analysis of the data, told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: He said this sub-atomic dance provided researchers with a ringside seat to the behaviour of possible new particles.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "And what we want to do now is go in and explore and find what new particles are waiting there.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: And to do that, what we need is more data," Cliff added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Dr Harry Cliff is one of a team of British scientists involved in the research The 28 countries involved in the project have agreed a £150m upgrade to this detector at the Large Hadron Collider (LHCb), which would increase the frequency of these decays tenfold.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "With that we can probe inside the zeptoverse and see what's waiting," Cliff said.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: But last year the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) agency, the government body in charge of research funding, announced that it was withdrawing its share of the money for the planned upgrade.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: It later announced cuts to several other particle physics and astronomy projects this Summer, including Jodrell Bank's iconic Lovell telescope .
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Although this research was led by scientists based in Cambridge, because of the cuts, Prof Tim Gershon, who leads the LHCb international collaboration, told BBC News that the UK's full involvement in the research would be in doubt.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "The UK is at risk of not being involved and making really major discoveries," he told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: She is reconsidering her future in light of the physics cuts.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "I love being here in the UK, but I am looking at jobs abroad because that seems to be where there are more opportunities at the moment," said Richardson-Slipper.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: She added that "lots" of her fellow researchers working in fundamental physics had already moved.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The cuts are being made despite an overall record increase in the science budget.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "It would be extraordinary to walk away from UK scientific leadership at this moment, damaging the future research programme and seriously damaging our hard-won international reputation," Cox said.

sentences.article_title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'

sentences.text: "There's no reason for them to have died needlessly for that reason." Siobhan Hawthorn says the team are "doing everything the can" to care for the sick birds Siobhan and the team have been working tirelessly to help revive the birds which include geese, ducks and swans.
sentences.article_title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'

sentences.text: Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Alphabet's stock market value fell sharply on Thursday, taking more than $500bn (£374bn) off its market value after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere however, with Intel shedding more than $130bn in value.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Amazon shares recovered some overnight losses, but were still down by 1.4% at the end of Friday trading.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Reddit stock plunged by 29%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by 18%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down." Many analysts have been debating the possibility of an AI bubble in the stock market.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The worry is that some tech firms will not be able to justify their sky-high valuations because the cost of building AI data centres and developing the software will end up being greater than the money they can make from it.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Kathleen Brookes, research director at trading firm XTB, said there have been many ups and downs in AI trade in recent months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "Investors have turned ruthless, punishing any signs of disappointment in [third quarter] earnings," she said.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "The AI trade has had a good run in recent years, but now investors want payback, and companies like Alphabet and Intel are in the crosshairs." However, stock market values for many of these companies remain well above where they were a year ago.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: While the Nasdaq closed 2.8% lower, it is up 7.8% over the last year.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Similarly Amazon is up nearly 8% over the past 12 months, while Alphabet is down 1.3%.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Brookes noted that November is typically a strong month for stocks.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "If we see AI stocks continue to struggle in the coming days, it could suggest the AI trade is past its peak, and investors will be looking for a new theme to drive markets," she said.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: British celebrity hairstylist and beauty brand entrepreneur John Frieda has died aged 75.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: Frieda became a firm favourite with celebrities throughout the 1960s and 1970s, and is known to have cut hair for clients including British model Twiggy, US First Lady Jackie Kennedy and Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: He was also known for the range of hair products bearing his name, and the iconic Purdey bowl cut which he created for The New Avengers actor Joanna Lumley in 1976.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: His death was announced by his hair salon in an Instagram post on Tuesday. , external "It is with heavy hearts that we share the news that our dear John passed away peacefully ….surrounded by his family", the statement said "John was more than a mentor to us; he was a true icon of the hair industry.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: He was the person who taught us everything, believed in us, and made us better.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: You will be forever in our hearts." Throughout his career, Frieda worked with other famous clients including Diana, Princess of Wales, Madonna, Nicole Kidman and Scarlett Johansson.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: After having gone into the family business, Frieda later joined Leonard Lewis's star-studded salon House of Leonard - famous for having created Twiggy's famous crop - becoming his assistant.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: He went on to work for fashion magazines British Vogue and Harper's Bazaar.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: In 1976, Frieda opened his own salon in central London which became massively successful and booked up months in advance as his reputation as an influential stylist grew.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: He subsequently opened branches across the world, including in Barbados, Ibiza and Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: In the 1990s, Frieda stepped back from cutting hair and concentrated on developing his own brand of hair products, including Frizz-Ease hair serum which he created in 1988.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: His business empire grew rapidly over the following decade as it expanded into the US and across the world.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: In 2002, he and his business partner Gail Federici sold the company to a Japanese conglomerate Kao for $450m (£334m).
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: Speaking to the British Beauty Council , external in June, Frieda gave his advice for future generation of British hairdressers.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "If you have a client in front of you, rather than thinking about the money or what you're getting from cutting their hair, just think about the action," he said.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "The reward is giving her the best haircut she's ever had.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: He was later married to Avery Agnelli, the widow of Fiat heir Giovanni Agnelli, with whom he had two children and  a stepdaughter.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: Frieda's step-daughter, Asia Agnelli Lagrange, shared a series of photos of them together down the years on Instagram , external alongside the caption: "Today we lost the best man to ever exist.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "When I was 16 and John worked as an assistant at Leonard's he would do my hair," she recalled.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "He was so great..." Cetera Lamb, creative director at Frieda's London salon said the industry had lost "a true legend, a real maverick in hairdressing".
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "For 50 years, he led our wonderful salon, leaving behind an incredible legacy of passion, creativity, vision and outstanding hairdressing.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: "We will continue in his honour, celebrating his achievements and keeping his memory, values, vision and love for great hairdressing alive.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: His legacy will live on through us, and we will make sure of that."
sentences.article_title: Celebrity hairstylist John Frieda dies aged 75

sentences.text: Phoebe Waller-Bridge is donating the London flat as part of the Writers' Block scheme Fleabag creator, writer and actress Phoebe Waller-Bridge is offering a rent-free flat in London for writers early in their careers.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: The 41-year-old has bought and donated the flat as part of a new theatre initiative Writers' Block, which aims to address the cost of London accommodation for playwrights from underprivileged backgrounds.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: She bought the flat specifically for writers who are starting out and are struggling to afford accommodation in the capital, and has donated its use alongside what the scheme called a "generous financial contribution".
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: Her flat will be provided without rent, with the resident paying bills only.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: Adolescence co-creator Jack Thorne – who wrote the films Wonder and Enola Holmes, as well as the Harry Potter And The Cursed Child stage play – is also providing financial backing to the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "I was lucky when I started out, my brother lived in Croydon and was able to put me up," he said.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "He did so, rather selflessly, for five years, before I moved to Luton and he got his peace.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "For many writers, the need for a roof makes writing impossible which is why this pilot is so important.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: If we want stories told about our complicated world, we need writers of every background writing them.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "If you're from privilege, your biggest problem is what to fill a page with.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: If you're not, so much of your struggle is about the need to survive." Other backers include playwright and screenwriter James Graham, who wrote stage shows including Ink, Quiz and Dear England, as well as Happy Valley creator Sally Wainwright and The Crown's Peter Morgan.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: Waller-Bridge's partner Martin McDonagh is also involved.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: He is best known for writing and directing films including Oscar and Bafta-winning The Banshees Of Inisherin and Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: Graham said the scheme tackled the class barrier facing writers and helped them avoid "giving up completely".
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "The industry's urgent pursuit of representation is still letting down the biggest area of under-representation of all, which is class," he said.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: "When I first made it to London, I slept on friends' floors and worked in call centres and bars while I wrote.
sentences.article_title: Fleabag star offers rent-free flat to new writers

sentences.text: Both schemes were created by Sofie Mason and Diana Jervis-Read.

sentences.text: A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the court saying the man's claim for an injunction was denied.

sentences.text: But the judge said a temporary injunction preventing the man from being named and the allegations published should remain in place, in order to allow the celebrity to appeal against the judgment, with anonymity and reporting restrictions remaining in force during the period allowed for any appeal.

sentences.text: ITN and the Guardian have said they believe it is in the public interest to publish allegations that the man abused his status to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".

sentences.text: The man, who denies the allegations, said any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself, and that the court should prevent any publication or broadcast.

sentences.text: The case raises highly unusual legal issues concerning whether a court should stop publication when an individual claims that a media investigation would lead to them inflicting harm on themselves.

sentences.text: The celebrity first asked the court in the summer to stop the publication of the investigation after journalists contacted him with allegations about this sexual activities with a large number of young women.

sentences.text: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC).
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Two decades later its share dropped to 40%.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: "What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Sanele Ntombela (left), seen here with his friends Tshiamo Mbange (centre) and Lwandle Dladla, is excited to cast his vote We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: "We face many challenges in Alexandra.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision.

sentences.text: "It makes no difference [whether I vote or not].

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere.

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections.
sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.article_title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

sentences.text: Joseph Kabila was a commander in the rebel alliance that brought his father to power in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1997, went on to succeed him as president and now, at the age of 55, he is a rebel leader once again.

sentences.text: Yiech Pur Biel (left) is leading the first ever refugee team at the Youth Olympics When he started running, Yiech Pur Biel had to compete barefoot.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics
